full_judgment:
5. Respondent Bank kept the matter pending for long time and did not inform the petitioner the fate of those recommendations. After receipt of the recommendations of the Parliamentary Committee in respect of the petitioner company respondent Bank sat in its 880th Board Meeting on 1st and 4th September, 2005 and took a resolution wherein it was decided, amongst others, to write off the entire liability of the petitioner in respect of the loan account and to return all its mortgaged properties by redemption and return all the charge documents. And on 19-10-2005 the Respondent Bank communicated a copy of the resolution to the petitioner. The petitioner company in turn accepted the proposals and informed the Bank addressing a letter dated 19-10-2005. After receiving the acceptance of the decision of the Board meeting Respondent Bank communicated a copy to the Respondent No.1 for its approval. Respondent No. 1 having received the Memo of the Respondent No.3 directed the latter to resolve the dispute with the petitioner with some findings. The Board of Directors then sought opinion of their legal advisors who opined against competence of the Bank in realizing the loan. Respondent No. 3 in spite of the fact chose not to implement the board resolution and pursued their suit against the petitioner. 

 11. Nonetheless the decision even if taken by the Bank is something to be implemented by the Bank itself. Bank Company is an independent identity. It has its objectives and internal policy to pursue. As the majority share is owned by the Government Sonali Bank is linked with public policy as well. Its Board of Directors has additional limitations in allowing total write off in respect of entire liabilities of its borrowers. In the instant case it appears from records that the Managing Director of the petitioner company is a politically powerful man. He, in association with other defaulters like him, moved heaven and earth for a write off and created tremendous pressure on the Bank management through different parliamentary committees, Hon'ble Speaker and the Ministry. The Bank management is seen to have sat on its Board Meeting and to take a decision which finally trailed away in the process of taking approval of the Ministry. Bangladesh Bank stood on the way saying that the capital amount was not condonable. Unfortunately for the petitioner, the Bank continued with the suit which suggests that the resolution did not mature into a decision.
